sections.heading: Working today
intro: All of this is covered by the offline suite — **5,932 tests, 5,800 passing, 1 failing, 131 skipped**. The 1 failing is not a feature: it is `test/web-ongoing.test.js` "5. the desktop margin", which fails the same way on a clean `origin/main` (2026-11-08). The 131 skipped need a real model and have not been run against the API for want of credit. The newest two are the flight check-in — a flight read out of one sentence, the offer raised by the sweep in the airport's own zone, nothing pressed before a yes, the seat read back off the page, and a payment wall handed back rather than paid — on the `claude-cli` backend (see below) on 2026-10-07. Before them, the standing commitment — "leg day tuesdays and fridays 7am" saved with the zone on it, a 7:12 with nothing from him answered by the real thing, the real time, his last session and "you hit 175 on squats last week. go 180.", "cant today" taken as the end of it, and a hurt knee getting no session and no advice — on that backend on 2026-10-07. Before it, the standing check-in — "check in with me every monday at 9 about the job search" read as one weekly series rather than one Monday reminder, a first firing about the search, what he said back carried into the second Monday in different words, and "stop checking in about that" ending it — on that backend on 2026-10-07. Before it, the hard line — six sentences seeking help toward harm refused before any model turn, seven innocent ones passed, two crisis messages read as crisis, one thread read for where it was going, and the whole path from a test number, all on that backend on 2026-10-06 (see the first rule under "The rules it keeps"). Before that, "where were we?" — a job mid-flight, asked for an update, answered with what is done before what is left before the one thing it needs, which is the difference between a status update and a demand. It passed twice on that backend on 2026-10-06. Next to it are the subscription flows — a year of receipts sorted into subscriptions and not-subscriptions, a `cancelling` row answered as not-yet rather than done, and a cancellation walked to the last button and pressed only on a real yes — on that backend the same day. On the machine this was last run on, `ffmpeg` is installed and `test/expressive.test.js` is green — the two failures that line used to carry are gone.
Newest first. One line each; open the fold for what is actually proved and what is not.

sections.heading: Built, but never run against the real thing
intro: Written carefully, offline-tested, and **unproven**. Do not treat any of it as working. `docs/unverified.md` is the full ledger, test by test. Newest first.

sections.heading: Not connected, and what you have to supply
intro: Reason says all of this itself when asked: the `capabilities` tool and `account_list` report every one of these as not connected, with what is missing. It starts up fine with none of them. Newest first; the fold is what you must supply.
outro: Picked, and genuinely not started: Reason's own email address, real bookings and checkouts with the exact total approved, group texts with polls, decks, and plug-in apps. `docs/features.md` has the agreed order under **Decided 2026-10-04**.

usecases.name: Checked in before you remember
usecases.hook: it watches the airline, offers, checks you in, hands back the pass
usecases.detail:
The card on the site, verbatim: *"check-in for your 7:15am to atlanta just opened. want me to do it?"* — *"yes pls, aisle if u can"* — *"done. you kept 14C."* — and a link. **It watches the airline, not your inbox, and it asks before it touches anything.**

**A flight gets in three ways and the model reads all three** — a sentence ("flying to atlanta friday at 7:15am on fixture air out of jfk, conf ABC123"), a confirmation email, a calendar event. No pattern-matching anywhere: what it read is stored, and **anything it worked out rather than was told is kept as a guess** and said as one. A card number sitting in the same booking email is refused outright, with nothing written down and nothing read back.

**The clock is the flight's, never this machine's.** 7:15 in New York opens 24 hours before 7:15 in New York, and the zone is stamped at save time off the departure airport — the suite runs the same flight through three zones in a process whose own clock is a fourth. A zone nobody knows and a time that is not a time are both refused rather than quietly read as UTC. The window is the airline's own where one is written down, 24h where it is not.

**The offer comes through the proactive sweep, not a timer** — inside your waking hours, one nudge per flight, inside the same daily budget as everything else, and it carries the real flight rather than "you have a flight". **Nothing is pressed without a yes on what the last screen actually says.** The seat only appears on that screen, so a yes collected earlier would be a yes to something nobody had seen; the yes is pinned to the flight as well as the details, so one flight's yes cannot be spent on another, and `browser_click` refuses anything labelled "Check in" by itself. **"Just check me in, stop asking" cannot be granted** — it is on the list of things no standing permission covers.

**"Done" is read off the page or it is not said.** Three things, separately, by code and not by the model: the checked-in words, a seat or a boarding position, and *their* name. Any one missing leaves the row at `checking_in` and the wording honest. A page confirming somebody else's booking is not a check-in; two travellers on one record stops and asks rather than saying you are both in; a screenshot of the screen the claim came off is kept with the flight. What you said in the same breath is carried — "aisle if u can" is kept on the flight *and* as a lasting preference, so the next flight starts out knowing it — and a middle seat after you asked for an aisle is said plainly rather than bought out of.

**It never spends your money.** A page wanting paying for a seat or a bag stops the commit *before* the press, which also means the yes is still sitting there unspent, and what comes back is the furthest point it reached with the one tap left for you — never a request for a card and never an offer to pay it. An airline that refuses self check-in on your fare is reported in the page's own words, unpressed. An app-only airline, a desk-only airline and one nobody has written down each say their own honest thing rather than guessing at a URL.

**The pass comes back as a Reason page** named off the row — "Boarding pass · ATL 7:15 AM", with the seat, the code and the airport's local time on it — and it says what it is not: Reason's own page, not the airline's scannable pass. All of it in `src/flights.js` and `src/airlines.js`, pinned by 56 tests in `test/flights.test.js` against a fake airline on 127.0.0.1.

**Against the real model** (`test/flow-flights.test.js`, `claude-cli`, 2026-10-07) the whole card ran unaided. One sentence became a row with the right zone and the right 24-hour mark; the sweep raised *"check-in for your 7:15am to atlanta out of jfk is open. want me to do it?"*; "yes pls, aisle if u can" came back *"I've found your trip but haven't checked you in yet. It's Omari Nyarko, JFK to ATL, friday 7:15am, seat 14C, and the page shows no fee."* with **nothing pressed**; "yeah go for it" pressed it exactly once and said *"You're checked in. You've got 14C, and the airline's page says that's an aisle seat."* On the paying fixture it stopped: *"I won't put a card in for the $35 bag, and that page doesn't let you check in without it"*, then offered the airport counter.

**What no test can prove: no real airline has ever been touched.** Every web step runs against `test/fixture-airline.js`, which is a fixture that cooperates. A real airline means a bot wall, a sign-in that expires, a seat map behind a modal and a page that changes next month, and none of that is settled here. Treat this as built, not working. `docs/unverified.md` has it test by test.

usecases.name: A file of theirs, handed back as a PDF
usecases.hook: their own resume out of their Drive, as a real attachment
usecases.detail:
From Omari's own thread on 2026-10-07: *"I asked Reason to give me my most recent résumé on the Drive and give it to me, but it kept saying it can't get it to me as a PDF."* Everything around the ask already worked — it could find the file, read the file, and write a brand new file out of its own words — and not one of those is what he asked for. `drive_send` is the missing middle: **that file**, in the format asked for, attached in the thread. It needs no yes, because it is their own file going to them.

Three routes, and the result says which one ran. A Google Doc, Sheet or Slides is **exported by Drive** (`files.export`). Something that is **already a PDF is sent byte for byte** — a resume Reason typed out again is not their resume. A Word file is **converted by Drive**: `files.copy` with a Doc mime type opens it as a Doc, that copy is exported as a PDF, and then the copy is deleted — which runs on the failing path too, with the delete's own outcome carried out to the ledger, so a copy that would not come back out is said in words with the name to look for rather than left in somebody's Drive to be found. The one route that writes in their Drive is the only one that checks for `drive.file`, against that file's own route, so a PDF that only had to be downloaded is never refused over a permission it never needed; a grant missing it gets the reconnect link the other Drive tools use.

**Every no names the yes.** Only PDF and Word come out: a Sheet or a deck can be a PDF and cannot be a Word file, because Google's export table puts the Word type on Documents and nowhere else. A PDF cannot become a Word file — that is OCR guessing at a layout, and what comes out is not the document. Nothing Pages, Keynote or Numbers wrote can be either, because Drive stores one and cannot open it; exporting from Pages on their own machine is the way, and that is the sentence they get. A file Drive labels `application/pdf` that does not start like one is refused rather than attached, because the type on an upload is whatever the uploader said it was.

And **"newest" is never "theirs"**: people keep a friend's resume, a client's contract, a form filled in for a parent. `owned_by_them` is the fact, the hand-back says whose it is, and one that is not theirs comes back refusing to let it be called theirs — "here's your resume" over somebody else's CV is the sentence that reaches a recruiter.

**Proved:** 21 offline tests against the fake Google — all three routes on real bytes, the whole conversion matrix including each refusal, the copy taken back out after an export Google refused, a copy that cannot be deleted owned up to by name, the wrong-account answer, the scope refusal, and a receipt with no file contents in it. Plus one live end-to-end run on the `claude-cli` backend on 2026-10-07 walking his exact sentence: it reached for `drive_send` and never `document_create`, picked his `.docx` over the newer resume in that Drive belonging to Kofi Mensah and said why unprompted — "The newest resume in your Drive is actually Kofi's, so I skipped it" — took the convert route, and the fake's own file list showed the temporary copy gone. **Not proved:** nothing here has run against a real Drive, so Google's export and copy behaviour is as documented and not as observed. See `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: A document, as a real file
usecases.hook: the blocks that make a page make a `.docx`, a `.pptx` or a PDF
usecases.detail:
A page is a link, and some things are not: a CV to upload, a deck for Monday, a one-pager to print. `document_create` takes the **same fixed blocks `page_create` takes** — so an answer the model has already shaped becomes a page *or* a file without being written twice, and without a second vocabulary to keep true — and writes a real file to this disk, then attaches it to the message in the thread. The PDF is deliberately not a third layout: it is Chromium printing the page renderer, the one already measured at 390×844, so a PDF looks like Reason and keeps looking like it when the page look changes.

Two things are refused by name rather than dropped, each saying what to do instead: a **tappable question**, which is a page block the owner presses and in a file is a list that does nothing, and a **picture in a `.docx` or `.pptx`**, because those writers embed no bytes and fetch no URLs, so it would arrive missing — the PDF is the one kind that carries an image, and the real-picture rule is unchanged. The file is Reason’s own, under the data directory and named from its row, which is what makes three promises mean the same bytes: a resend attaches it, an export carries it base64 with its checksum, a delete unlinks it, and the retention window takes file and row together.

Nothing claims a send that did not happen. The bytes are made before any row exists, so a renderer that falls over leaves nothing behind; a failed upload still made the document and says it did not go; a channel that cannot carry an attachment gives the owner a keyed `/f/{id}` link instead, a terminal gets the path, and `capabilities` reports `documents` as live **only where a file can actually be carried**. Sending one to anybody but the owner is held to the rules for texting that person: an explicit yes with the number and the document said back, the undo window, and that yes is not spendable on a different document.

**Proved:** 32 offline tests on real bytes — a Word file with the content in it, a deck with a slide per section, the PDF out of the page renderer with no animation and no link tags, the refusals, the keyed download, the export, the delete and the retention sweep. Plus one live end-to-end run on the `claude-cli` backend on 2026-10-07: asked for a pour-over coffee guide and then "send me that as a pdf", it made exactly one document, a 151,656-byte PDF titled "Pour over coffee", carried as a single message with the file attached, and the words were read back out of the PDF itself. **Not proved:** nobody has opened a Reason `.docx` in Word or a `.pptx` in Keynote on a real device — the OOXML writers are hand-rolled and have only been read back by the tests that wrote them — and the live server has not been restarted onto this code. See `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: Check-ins that keep coming back
usecases.hook: every monday about the job search; it tracks what you said last time
usecases.detail: Reason’s reminders were all one-offs. Now anything standing — "check in with me every monday about the job search", "remind me every day at 7 to work out", "every weekday morning ask me what’s on", "every two weeks ask if i’ve invoiced" — is **one arrangement that keeps going until you stop it**. It is one row, and **every firing is an ordinary reminder** pointing back at it, so the send-then-claim rule, the three tries, the "a reminder was missed" line and the list of what Reason has set and not yet sent all work on a check-in unchanged. **It tracks from what you say back.** The first thing you say after a check-in is kept as the report — by code, not by the model, because it has to still be true in six weeks — and the next one is handed it: "last monday you said two applications were out, any replies?" rather than the same line every week. Three things are code’s and not the model’s. **The maths**: occurrences are walked in local days, so "every monday at 9" is 9 o’clock on both sides of the November clock change (169 real hours apart, not 168), "every weekday" skips the weekend, and "every month on the 31st" skips February rather than inventing a date. **Quiet hours**: nothing fires between 23:00 and 08:00 where you are unless you named that time yourself. **No backlog**: three Mondays with the laptop shut produce one check-in, for the newest, and the older ones are gone. Stopping is a sentence: "stop checking in about that" ends it, "pause the workout reminders" holds it and resumes from the next one after that moment, and a bare "stop" with more than one running gets asked which rather than guessed at. Every one of them leaves a receipt with the schedule in the words you were told. Ten running per person (`REASON_MAX_SERIES`), counted in the database. All of it in `src/series.js`, pinned by `test/series.test.js`. **Against the real model** (`test/flow-series.test.js`, `claude-cli`, 2026-10-07) the Monday ask became one weekly series rather than one reminder, and the second Monday opened "morning. last monday you had two applications out, has either one gotten back to you?". **What tests cannot prove**: nothing here has run on the live Reason or over real days on a real phone — "a series that survives several real fires" is exactly the claim a fake clock cannot make. See `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: Organising their Drive
usecases.hook: folders, moves, renames and the bin; a batch is proposed first
usecases.detail: "I should also be able to organize." Reading a Drive and tidying one are two different Google permissions, and `drive.metadata` is the new one — so every connection made before today is answered with "reconnect and I can organise it", with the link, rather than a 403, and the check runs before the confirm gate so nobody is asked to approve something that was never going to work. Above that: one file moves on the asking; **more than one is proposed first** in counts and names and moves only on a yes pinned to that exact set; fifty is a refusal rather than a silent first-fifty; a failed move **stops** and says how many had moved; binning and sharing-with-a-person both ask and then wait out the undo window; and **no permanent delete exists** — a test walks every file in `src/` to keep it that way. Sharing reaches only files Reason made itself, which is said as a permission with the link offered, never as "Google refused it". `drive_upload` accepts only paths under `REASON_DATA_DIR`, resolved through `realpath`, which is what stops a sentence in somebody's message pointing it at private files. Walked live with the real model on 2026-10-07 against a fake Google: "make a folder in my drive called Taxes 2026" was just done, "ok now move my receipts into it" came back as “I only found 2 receipts in your drive, the dentist one and the plumber one. Want me to move both into Taxes 2026?” with nothing moved, and “yes” moved exactly those two and left the unrelated doc alone — no file id in any of the three replies. Never run against a real Google Drive, and the scope is not on Google's Data Access page yet; see `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: The calendar check, and the event it confirms
usecases.hook: clashes shown as a tradeoff; nothing called "added" before it is read back
usecases.detail: "A bare 'create event' action leaves me managing the rest." So putting something on a calendar is four things rather than one. **The diary is read first**: anything overlapping the proposed window comes back with its title, time and place, nothing is created, and the person is shown the tradeoff in their own words — "that's over your 2pm with Sarah, move it or keep both?" — and picks. Going ahead takes their decision carried back on the next call. A clear time is created in that same call with no extra question. **A time has to be a real time**: "Tuesday at 3" is refused rather than resolved against the server's clock, and so is a wall-clock time when neither Google nor the person has ever said which zone they are in — the tool names the question to ask instead of guessing. **Nothing is "added" on the strength of a 200**: every create and every time change is read back from Google by id and compared, and an event that landed an hour out is reported as exactly that. **A correction corrects**: "make it 4 instead" changes that same event id, and a second create of the same thing on the same day is refused and handed the id. What a conflict check cannot do is a judgement about which of two things matters more — that is always the person's. Walked live with the real model on 2026-10-06 against a fake Google: a clash over a coffee got “I haven't added it yet … want to move one of them, or keep both?”, “keep both” made exactly one event, and “actually make it 4pm” moved that same one. Never run against a real Google calendar; see `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: Nobody uses it to hurt anybody
usecases.hook: every text screened before the model; harm gets no turn at all
usecases.detail: A separate narrow model call reads every message anybody sends, with the last few lines of the thread, before the model sees it. On **harm** — planning or carrying out violence, a weapon, a bomb, a poison, a nerve agent, drugging somebody, stalking, anything sexual involving a child, breaking into accounts; whatever the framing — there is no model turn: a refusal written in code goes back, the thread keeps it, and it is a ledger row and a strike. Three strikes in a day pause that person and tell the master the count and the kind, never the words. Borderline reads, a person in crisis, and a screen that could not run all get a turn with every outward tool refused; crisis gets a guaranteed crisis line and never a strike. No off switch.

usecases.name: Why, not just what
usecases.hook: the reason you gave is kept and it reorders the options
usecases.detail: "I want to move" is one job; "to save money" and "for a shorter commute" are two different jobs out of the same five flats. A reason you state is its own row — the subject, the goal in your terms, and **your own sentence, verbatim** — kept apart from facts and from preferences, because a fact is what stays true about you and a reason is what you are trying to achieve. It outlives the task it was said on, arrives on the sheet of every later job on that subject, and the model is told to rank by it and to say so in one short clause. Two things are code's: a reason with no sentence behind it is refused, so an invented motive cannot start sorting your options; and a correction **supersedes** rather than overwrites, so the old one is kept as replaced and stays checkable. It is a goal and never a permission.

usecases.name: Memory you can correct
usecases.hook: numbered sections for everything it holds; text back a correction and it sticks
usecases.detail: "What do you remember about me" is one page with a number on every line: what you told it, what it is **guessing** (labelled as guesses, never said back as fact, and only ever promoted by you saying the thing), what you have turned down and why, **why you said you are doing things**, and what it may do without asking. Text back "#4's wrong, she's my cousin" and it changes that one line — and stops saying the old version anywhere, including in things it has already said.

usecases.name: Taste
usecases.hook: a no is kept in your words and shapes every later pick
usecases.section: What it may do without asking
usecases.detail: When you turn an option down it keeps your reason, in your words, with what kind of no it was, and every later pick is made knowing it. It is a preference and never a permission: nothing it learns this way lets it spend anything or send anything.

usecases.name: Noticing things first
usecases.hook: goes looking in mail and calendar, one catch a day
usecases.detail: It goes looking, every couple of hours, at a connected mailbox and calendar: a meeting that moved deep in a thread, a bill sitting unread, a reply somebody is waiting on. Anything they already handled is checked against the live mailbox and never raised. One unprompted catch a day, counted in the database, one nudge per thing, sent at the moment it is useful rather than in a batch, nothing in their night, and the three-question bar in front of all of it. How much initiative they want is theirs — the moment it matters, one batched line a day, or only ever when they ask — and none of it is permission to act for them. See **Noticing things first** above. The judgement side has only ever been exercised with a fake model: whether its sense of "worth interrupting somebody for" is any good is in `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: Subscriptions
usecases.hook: a year of receipts, a monthly total, and a real cancellation
usecases.detail: Read a year of their receipts and come back with what is actually going out, keep the list, show it as a page with a monthly total, and cancel one — on the web with their own saved sign-in, or as a written request from their own address. Both behind their explicit yes, and nothing is ever called cancelled until something confirms it. See **Subscriptions** above.

usecases.name: Their Drive
usecases.hook: find a file, read a Doc, Sheet, Slides or a real PDF
usecases.detail: Against the same fake Google: find a file by its name or by what is inside it, read a Doc, a Sheet (first sheet, and it says so), Slides, a text or html file, **and a PDF — read on this machine, against real PDFs built in the tests**, including a real password-protected one that is refused and a real scan that is named as a scan — make a new Google Doc and send back the link. A Word file, an image and a folder each get a plain sentence saying Reason cannot read that one, with the link. Nothing is deleted, shared or edited, because the scopes for that are not asked for. And **an existing Google connection is not a Drive connection**: Drive is its own tap, and asking for it adds a permission without costing them the ones they have. Nothing has been sent to Google. See **Their Drive** and `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: Reminders and timers
usecases.hook: real turns at real times, one-off or standing; fired once the message is out
usecases.detail: Reminders and timers that fire real turns at real times. **A timer counts as fired once its message is in the outbox, not before**: a turn that throws or times out leaves it due, it is tried again on the next sweep (three tries in all, `REASON_TIMER_MAX_ATTEMPTS`), the reply goes out under a key that belongs to that timer so retrying cannot text twice, and if it still cannot be got out they get one line saying a reminder was missed and what it was. Until 2026-10-06 the timer was marked fired first, and a turn killed after the Mac slept took the reminder with it — not sent, not retried, nobody told. `Runtime.tick`, pinned by `test/timer-claim.test.js`. A reminder can also be **standing** rather than one-off — every Monday, every weekday morning, every two weeks — in which case one series row keeps making them, one at a time, and each one is an ordinary timer with all of the above still true of it. See “Check-ins that keep coming back”.

usecases.name: Gmail, per person and as many accounts as they have
usecases.hook: read, send, bin across every account, attached PDFs included
usecases.detail: Against a fake Google server built from their docs: a link each person taps, tokens stored and refreshed against their own conversation and their own address, reading across every account they connected with each result labelled, sending and binning gated on the real recipients, the whole body **and the sending account**, an email's own words treated as data and never as an instruction, and a dead connection reported as needing a reconnect rather than retried. **A PDF attached to an email is read** — against real PDFs built in the tests and really put through this machine's own reader — with the bytes fetched only for the one file asked about, a real scan named as a scan, a really encrypted one refused, and an instruction written inside the document flagged and unable to become a yes. Nothing has been sent to Google — the client id and secret are on the machine and have deliberately never been used. See `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: A message Reason starts reaches the phone
usecases.hook: reminders and task news go to the thread, not the log
usecases.detail: A reminder, a task's news, a watcher or a picked-up thread goes to the thread that conversation lives in. Until 2026-10-05 these had no channel and were printed into the server's log instead — written, recorded as said, and never texted. `src/deliver.js`, pinned by `test/deliver.test.js`.

usecases.name: Research, with a real pick
usecases.hook: many searches, sources read in full, then a recommendation
usecases.detail: Several different searches, the best sources read in full, a source log of what each one said and when, then a recommendation with what would change it. Capped so one question cannot run away, and it says when a cap cut it short. A big question runs as a durable task. The provider interface and the whole flow are offline-tested against a fake provider and fixture pages; the Tavily request shape is tested against its documented contract but **has never been sent to Tavily** — no key. **Reddit is never fetched** (its robots.txt forbids everyone); what threads say arrives as search snippets, labelled as snippets.

usecases.name: Finding out what is in a video
usecases.hook: a link becomes timestamped lines, and says what produced them
usecases.detail: A YouTube link (and many other video sites) → the title, channel, length, description, chapters and what is in it as timestamped lines. It reads the captions when there are any; a long one is cut and says which stretch is missing, and a follow-up reads that stretch. An age gate, a private video or a region block comes back as the reason. Every result says which of three things produced it, so "watched" is only ever said when something really watched. Proved against real YouTube videos as well as offline fixtures; see the manual checks in `docs/unverified.md`. The **video model** tiers — watching a YouTube link, and transcribing audio from anywhere else — are built and offline-tested but need `GEMINI_API_KEY`. The audio-only download and the delete-after are proved for real; nothing has ever been sent to Google.

usecases.name: Saved sign-ins, site playbooks, a daily spending limit and Spotify
usecases.hook: browsing free, the committing click gated, tokens never shared
usecases.detail: Against local fixture pages and a fake Spotify server: browsing is free, the committing click is gated whatever the site calls it, a changed total asks again, and one person's sign-in or token is never usable from another's conversation. No real site has been signed in to and nothing has been sent to Spotify.

usecases.name: Telling somebody what's new, in passing
usecases.hook: one live thing, one a day, never while a confirm is open
usecases.detail: The gates are code's: nothing unverified is ever put in front of the model, nothing is mentioned that is not live for that person, one thing per reply and one per person per day, never while a confirmation is open, never on a message Reason started, and never to somebody who arrived after the feature did. Marked heard only once the reply really went out. What no test can prove is the part the model owns — whether it actually reads the moment right and writes one casual line rather than a pitch. See `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: Messages arriving the way people actually send them
usecases.hook: two texts are one turn; a photo arrives as a picture
usecases.detail: Two texts seconds apart are one turn; the parts of one iMessage (a pasted link and its preview card) are one message rather than three; a photo or screenshot reaches the model as a picture to look at, and anything that cannot be read is explained once, by name, instead of being called "blank". Against the real failing shapes from a real phone.

usecases.name: Photos, voice notes and links
usecases.hook: HEIC converted, voice transcribed, and a row for each
usecases.section: What they send: photos, voice notes, links
usecases.detail: An iPhone HEIC converted before anything looks at it, a voice note transcribed and answered as the words in it, a link sent as its own bubble, and a row for every one of them saying what was actually got out of it. See **What they send** above.

usecases.name: Hand back the furthest point
usecases.hook: a filled form and the one tap left, never a bare couldn't do it
usecases.detail: A job's sheet carries a `furthest` record: what was reached, the shape it is in (a filled form, a ready draft, a partial result, a browser sitting on the right page), a link if there is one, what is already filled in, the ONE thing left for them to do, and why it stopped — from a fixed list. Append-only; the newest is what gets handed back. Three parts are code's: a job that got anywhere cannot be closed `failed` or set `blocked` with none of it handed over (one `task_update` clears it, and a job that produced nothing is refused nothing); a link on a hand-back is fetched first and a dead one refused; and when a browser walk stops — the commit click the gate will not press, a step the site refuses, or the ask for the yes itself — the address reached and the filled fields are read off the page and written down by code. Passwords are never recorded and a card-shaped value is recorded as filled with the digits withheld. The link is handed back as the page it is, never as the form it is not. The open-work page shows it on a stuck job, with the link as a link. The money guards on that last button stop the same way — a total the yes does not cover, a page past a standing permission, a missing limit, the install's daily ceiling — and each refusal carries where it got to with its own reason. What code cannot do is make the reply lead with it, so that was run: on 2026-10-06, against a fixture booking site on the claude-cli backend the live Reason runs on, the real model walked to the last button, was stopped, and said "the form is filled with your name, Omari, and 555-0100 … want me to hit confirm?" — with no apology in it at all.

usecases.name: Cancelling a subscription
usecases.hook: fifteen services' flows read off their help pages, none walked
usecases.detail: The registry in `src/cancel-routes.js` was read off fifteen services' own help pages on 2026-10-06 and **not one of those flows has been walked**. No account here has ever been cancelled and nothing in Reason has ever pressed one of those buttons: the web rail is proved end to end against a fixture service on 127.0.0.1 (a sign-in, a retention offer, a two-step cancellation, a confirmation number), and the mail rail against the fake Google. On 2026-10-06 that fixture rail was also walked by the **real model**, unaided: it read the retention offer and said so, clicked past it, stopped at "Finish Cancellation", said the $5 fee and the end date back, asked, and pressed only after a yes in his own words. What a fixture cannot settle is whether Netflix's page still says "Finish Cancellation", whether any of these sites will talk to an automated browser at all, and whether a retention wall sits somewhere the registry does not know about. Four of the entries do not document their last button and say so; one could not be read at all and is `unknown`.

usecases.name: The Bland call provider
usecases.hook: written from their docs, field by field; no phone has rung
usecases.detail: Written from Bland's own docs (`POST /v1/calls`, `GET /v1/calls/{id}`, `GET /v1/calls/{id}/recording`, their webhook-signing page), read 2026-10-05, with the page named next to every field in `src/calls/bland.js`. There is no `BLAND_API_KEY` on this machine, so **no phone has ever rung**: 38 tests drive it with an injected `fetch` and assert on the exact URL and body. What only a real call can settle — that the opening line is really spoken word for word, that it really declines when asked for a card, that a recording really comes back, that a webhook really arrives — is all listed in `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: Handing work to the builders on this machine
usecases.hook: one real one-step hand-over ran; everything harder has not
usecases.section: Handing work to the builders on this machine
usecases.detail:
**One real hand-over has run end to end**, and that is the whole of it. 59 offline tests cover the switch, the master-only gate, the brief, what is read back off disk, the states, the pages, the quiet window and the delete; none of them start a process. On 2026-10-05 one real job was handed to a real `openclaw` session against a scratch data dir: the detached runner started, the builder read the brief and appended `progress`, `detail` and `done` lines in the shapes it was asked for, the sentinel landed with exit 0, the reply parsed out of the real envelope, the state settled to `done` from what the builder wrote, and both pages built. So the path works once, for a one-step job.

What has **not** been run: a job long enough to be swept while mid-turn, a builder asking a question and the answer getting back to it, a risky action going through the gate to a real builder, two jobs at once, a restart mid-build, and the text itself (no channel is connected on this machine). Every state and page for all of those is offline-tested and none of them is proven.

usecases.name: Buying things
usecases.hook: an AgentCard organization; the person stores a card once
usecases.detail: An organization from [app.agentcard.sh](https://app.agentcard.sh): put its client id and secret in `AGENTCARD_CLIENT_ID` and `AGENTCARD_CLIENT_SECRET`. Then each person taps the vault link Reason sends once and stores a card on AgentCard's own page, locked with their own passkey — Reason never sees the number. For the webhooks, register `{REASON_PUBLIC_URL}/agentcard/webhook` as an endpoint and put the secret it hands back in `AGENTCARD_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; **the route fails closed without it**, like every other inbound hook here. Everything still works without the webhook — a stored card is noticed by reading the vault session instead — but the person is then not told when their card lands or when an approval is declined. **Sandbox credentials stop at the confirm by design**: the loop and the cart are identical to production and the confirm comes back `declined` with `decline_code: sandbox_mode`, because a sandbox card cannot pay a real shop.

usecases.name: Google Drive
usecases.hook: two scopes on the Data Access page, then one tap each
usecases.detail: The same OAuth client, plus **two scopes added on its Data Access page** — `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly` and `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file` — and the **Drive API enabled** on the project. Google rejects an app whose code requests a scope not declared there, so until those two are on the page a Drive connect fails at Google's own screen rather than here. Nothing goes in `.env`: the code side is built. Then **each person taps a Drive link of their own** — connecting Gmail does not connect Drive, so everybody already on needs one more tap, and nobody has to redo their mail. `drive.readonly` is a **restricted** scope, which is the same review class Gmail already put this app in, so it changes the verification work not at all; `drive.file` is non-sensitive. See **Their Drive**.

usecases.section: Handing work to the builders on this machine
usecases.detail: `REASON_REMOTE_BUILD=1` plus an [OpenClaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw) install on the same machine (`REASON_OPENCLAW_BIN`, `REASON_OPENCLAW_AGENT`). With it off there is no such tool and nobody is told one exists; Reason still writes code for anyone who asks, it just has nobody to hand the running of it to.

usecases.name: Phone calls
usecases.hook: a Bland account at $0.14 a connected minute; caps hold it
usecases.detail: A [Bland](https://app.bland.ai) account, then `REASON_CALL_PROVIDER=bland` and `BLAND_API_KEY`. Their published Start-plan rate is **$0.14 a connected minute**, free to sign up; `REASON_MAX_CALLS_PER_DAY` and `REASON_MAX_CALL_MINUTES_PER_DAY` are what stop one person running that up. Optional: `BLAND_FROM_NUMBER` (without it Bland dials from its own pool), and `BLAND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` from their dashboard so the call-finished webhook is verified by signature rather than only by the unguessable token in its URL. With no `REASON_PUBLIC_URL` there is no webhook at all and outcomes are polled, which Bland's own docs call the right answer rather than a workaround. `docs/call-providers.md` compares the alternatives.

usecases.name: Web search, and therefore research
usecases.hook: a Tavily key; 1,000 free credits is ~200 questions a month
usecases.detail: `TAVILY_API_KEY`, from [app.tavily.com](https://app.tavily.com). **1,000 API credits a month, free, no credit card** (their docs, read 2026-10-05). A basic search costs 1 credit, so that is about 1,000 searches a month, and one research run spends up to 5 of them — roughly 200 questions a month on the free tier. Past it: **$0.008 a credit** pay-as-you-go, or $30/mo for 4,000. Reading the pages afterwards is free (a plain fetch, not a Tavily extract). Without it, `capabilities` says search is not connected, `research` refuses rather than guessing, and Reason reads a page whose address it can name itself and says that is all it did. Brave Search is the alternative and is **not wired**: its free tier is $5 of monthly credit on a billing plan.

usecases.name: Watching a video, or reading one with no captions
usecases.hook: a Gemini key; ~0.45 cents a minute to watch
usecases.detail: `GEMINI_API_KEY`, from aistudio.google.com. Per Google's docs (2026-10-05): a video is ~100 tokens per second at default media resolution, audio is 32 tokens per second, so on `gemini-3.8-flash` at $0.75 / M input that is roughly **0.45 cents a minute to watch** and **0.14 cents a minute to listen**, plus output. Free tier capped at 8 hours of YouTube a day. Public videos only. Capped at `REASON_VIDEO_MAX_MINUTES` (60) a video and cached per video and tier. No ffmpeg needed. Without it, a caption-less video comes back saying there is no way to know what is in it, and Reason says that.

usecases.detail: Nothing but `yt-dlp` on the machine (`pipx install yt-dlp`, `brew install yt-dlp`, or the standalone binary), or `REASON_YTDLP_BIN` pointed at it. No key, no account. usecases.name: It notices when you skip
usecases.hook: a standing commitment; the time goes past, one nudge, and the session handed over
usecases.detail: A thing you say you *do* — **"leg day tuesdays and fridays 7am"** — is a commitment rather than a reminder, and the difference is that **nothing happening is the news**. So there is no timer behind one: the sweep reads the rows and the clock, and an occurrence with no log against it at ten past seven *is* the event. The zone is stamped on the row when you set it, so a 7am is 7am where you are, and stays 7am on both sides of the clock change. **The nudge is one text and then the session.** It goes out through `src/notice.js` like everything unprompted — inside your waking hours, one per occurrence and never a second, and silent the moment you have already said you went. It names the real thing and the real time ("leg day. you said 7 and it's 7:12 👀"), hands over **your last session** with every exercise's sets and reps, and then **the figure you really hit with a higher one to go for**. That last part is the whole point: a nudge on its own leaves you a decision, and removing the decision is the help. A schedule *you* set does not spend the day's one unprompted text — but it is still one nudge, and the hour you named carries its own permission and nothing wider, so a 5am commitment gets its 5:10 text and your night is otherwise still your night. **Every number comes off a row you logged, and there is no other source.** With nothing logged it says it has not got last time's numbers and asks for today's instead of naming a weight — a made-up 185 is Reason inventing your own body back at you. **No shame, written as refusals rather than manners**: no count, no streak, no days-since, no disappointment, no asking why. "cant today" is the end of it — one warm line, logged, no re-ask, and nothing more that morning however many sweeps run. Something hurting gets no plan, no numbers and no advice of any kind. **Three missed in a row is a wrong schedule and not a reason to push**: it asks once whether to move it or drop it, and either answer is a good one. All of it is read as meaning by the model — "omw", "already went", "cant today", "move it to 8", "my knee hurts" — and nothing anywhere in it matches a pattern. What you do on a schedule is **on the memory page with your numbers under it**, and correcting it really is one text: saying the new time keeps every session already logged against it. All of it in `src/commitment.js`, pinned by 43 tests in `test/commitment.test.js`. **Against the real model** (`test/flow-habit.test.js`, `claude-cli`, 2026-10-07) the card ran word for word: at 7:12 with nothing from him, *"leg day. you said 7 and it's 7:12 👀"*, then *"squats 4x8, rdl 3x10 @ 135, lunges 3x12"*, then *"you hit 175 on squats last week. go 180."*; "omw" got the whole session back and *"squats were 175 last time, so 180 today."*; "squats 185x8" was logged and answered *"185 for 8, that's 5 more than i told you to go for 💪"*; and the next one, read off that log, opened *"you hit 185 on squats last week. go 190."* The same run proved a no is a no: "cant today" got no guilt and no second nudge, and "my knee hurts" got no session and no advice. **What tests cannot prove**: no real morning has happened. Every clock in every test is the fake one, so "it noticed a skip on a real Tuesday" is exactly the claim none of this makes. See `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: A restart does not cost you your message
usecases.hook: a turn killed mid-answer by a restart is put back, not apologised for
usecases.detail:
Every `systemctl restart reason` used to throw away whatever turn was running and tell the person their message had broken. From the live journal on 2026-10-17: `Stopping reason.service`, then one second later `the CLI returned no JSON (exit 143)` and a `turn_failed`, and Omari got "ugh — that one broke on my end partway through" for a message that was not broken. The `requests` row for his text was left `dropped`, and the box was restarted seven times that day.

A turn that dies while the process is stopping is now unfinished rather than failed, and the difference is proved rather than guessed: 143 is 128+15, so a child that exits 143 or dies of a signal outright resolves `interrupted`, and `Runtime.stopping` covers a backend with no exit code to read. Nothing is said to them — "that broke on my end" would be a lie and would also lose the reply, asking them to repeat a message still sitting on disk. What the turn took it puts back: the messages return under their original `arrived_at`, so a burst goes back whole and in order, and with `quietMs: 0`, because they already waited one quiet window and a restart must not charge them a second. The `requests` rows that turn opened are dropped, so nobody is asked the same thing twice. `shutdown` waits on `Router.idle()` after `Runtime.idle()`, so the putting-back lands before the process goes.

`src/channels/router.js`, `src/backends/cli.js` and `src/serve.js`, pinned by nine tests in `test/restart-safe.test.js` — three of them spawning a real child and killing it for real, because the claim is about what a dying child reports and a mock would only prove the mock agreed.
